subject: DPA: certified erase / tombstone notification workflow — evidence & timeline
messages:
From: Sara Li <dpo@acme-corp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Cloud Legal <legal@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redlines: certified erasure & backup/tombstone notifications

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the earlier call. Attaching Acme's redlined DPA (ACME_DPA_redline_v3.pdf). Our primary open point is the deletion/certification language and how Redwood will evidence erasure for production data, backups/snapshots, and ephemeral caches. Specific asks: 

- A statement that Redwood will provide a certificate of erasure for on-demand delete requests within X days after completion.
- Maximum allowable retention for backups/snapshots after customer-initiated deletion (we propose 30 days) and a requirement to remove copies from all onshore/offshore backups.
- Clarify whether log/telemetry used for incident troubleshooting is excluded and for how long.

Can you confirm whether you can accept an explicit 30-day backup window and provide a template for the certificate of erasure? If not, please propose alternative language.

Thanks,
Sara Li
DPO, Acme Corp

Attachment: ACME_DPA_redline_v3.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <dpo@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Jun 2029 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines: certified erasure & backup/tombstone notifications

Hi Sara — thanks for the redlines and for outlining the asks. Looping Marcus and Laura who own ops and legal syncs respectively. Quick notes from our side: 

- We can commit to providing a certificate of erasure for customer-initiated deletions. Our standard turnaround for a certification PDF is 10 business days after erasure completes — we can shorten this to 7 business days if you need a faster SLA in the DPA.

- Backups/snapshots: we have two relevant copies to consider: hot snapshots (fast recovery, overwritten quickly) and cold backups (longer-term archival). For operational resilience we typically hold cold backups for up to 60 days before scheduled pruning. For a DPA carveout we can offer a 30-day deletion window for production data and primary snapshots, with a contractual commitment to purge cold archival copies within 60 days and provide evidence. If Acme needs a hard 30-day maximum for all copies, we need to confirm acceptable risk tradeoffs (brief RTO/RPO impact).

- Logs/telemetry: we separate telemetry used for platform health (retained 90 days default) from customer payload logs (we purge per-customer retention settings). We can offer scoped exceptions for incident investigation with documented access controls and a requirement to redact customer content unless explicitly required.

I'll attach a concise response PDF (redline_response_v1.pdf) with proposed DPA language options (Option A: 30-day primary/snapshot + 60-day archival purge proof; Option B: uniform 30-day purge across all stores but with limited SLA for restore). Marcus — can you confirm the technical feasibility of producing an erase manifest and the earliest evidence artifacts we can provide?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline_response_v1.pdf (pdf, 35KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Sara Li <dpo@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines: certified erasure & backup/tombstone notifications

Hi all — technical follow-up. Short summary of what we can produce as evidence and the timeline: 

- Erase manifest: a machine-readable record listing the object ids and deletion timestamps across tiers (primary, snapshot, cold-archive). We can generate this within 48 hours of completing the purge operation for primary and snapshot stores. For cold-archive (deep storage) we kick an asynchronous purge job; manifest availability depends on vendor/region (typically 7–30 days).

- Certificate of erasure: operations will produce a signed PDF containing the purge job IDs, timestamps, and scope (bucket/partition identifiers). Draft template attached (erase_manifest_template.xlsx) to show fields.

- Backups: if we accept a 30-day uniform window, we will need to schedule immediate purge jobs across all regions and potentially disable cross-region replication for the affected tenant while purge completes. That increases the operational blast radius for restores by making it time-sensitive.

- Telemetry/logs: for incident traces we can produce redacted extracts that demonstrate deletion activity without exposing customer content. Access to full raw telemetry will require a legal hold process.

Operational ask: if Acme needs 30 days across the board, please confirm whether you expect: (a) immediate disable of replication and purge start on signature; or (b) a 30-day countdown that allows short-lived recovery within that window. Option (a) reduces residual copies faster but reduces recovery options.

--Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Infra Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachment: erase_manifest_template.xlsx (excel, 12KB)

From: John Doe <john.doe@meganet.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Li <dpo@acme-corp.com>, Acme Cloud Legal <legal@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2029 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines: certified erasure & backup/tombstone notifications

Kimberly / Marcus,

Thanks — Acme prefers Option A with a firm 30-day maximum for all primary and snapshot copies and a 60-day maximum for cold archive, provided Redwood supplies a certificate and erase manifest within 7 business days for primary/snapshot purges and within 30 days for cold-archive proof. We are okay with a short operational disclaimer about RTO/RPO if replication must be disabled to meet the 30-day target.

Action items from our side:
- I uploaded a refreshed set of redlines to the shared folder and added a short comment on the certificate format. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0A12acme-dpa-examples
- We would like Redwood to update the DPA and send a DocuSign-ready copy. If you can provide the DocuSign template link, we will circulate internally.

One more ask: for audits, can Redwood commit to maintaining an immutable audit log of purge operations for at least 12 months? We don't need content — only metadata about purge actions (who, when, job id).

Thanks,
John Doe
Counsel, MegaNet (external counsel supporting Acme)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <dpo@acme-corp.com>, John Doe <john.doe@meganet.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2029 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines: certified erasure & backup/tombstone notifications

Thanks everyone — agreed path forward. Summary / proposed compromise for the DPA language (we will send a DocuSign-ready redline later today):

1) Certification SLA: Redwood to provide a signed certificate of erasure for customer-initiated deletions within 7 business days of completion for primary and snapshot purges, and within 30 calendar days for cold-archive purges.

2) Retention windows: primary and snapshot copies to be purged within 30 calendar days of deletion request; cold-archive copies to be purged within 60 calendar days. We will document the purge job ids and include them in the certificate.

3) Replication: Redwood may disable cross-region replication for the affected tenant during purge to meet the 30-day target; this will be noted in the certificate if performed.

4) Audit metadata: Redwood will retain immutable purge metadata (job id, timestamp, operator id, region) for 12 months and make metadata available to Acme on reasonable request for audits. Metadata will not include customer content.

5) Telemetry: platform telemetry used for operations will be redacted; raw content traces will be preserved only under legal hold.

Next steps: Laura, can you prepare the DocuSign template and attach the final redline (we will start from redline_response_v1.pdf)? Marcus, ops — please stage the erase_manifest template as an accepted artifact and confirm the manifest fields we will publish. Sara/John — if that matrix looks acceptable we will push the updated DPA to DocuSign and route for signature.

Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference
